sents.t: Last week, I had my first real problem as a manager.
Tina and Jake both asked for the same Saturday off.
Tina’s daughter has a dance recital that day, and Jake has bought tickets to a concert in Riverside.
“I asked first,” Tina said.
“I’ve worked every Saturday this month.”
“But I bought my ticket in May,” Jake answered.
“I haven’t had a Saturday off since spring!”
After that, they stopped talking to each other, and the store felt tense.
Even customers noticed it.
I didn’t know what to do, so I called Mr. Lee.
“You can’t make everyone happy,” he said.
“But you can be fair. Listen to both sides, and look at the facts.”
So I checked the schedule.
Tina was right: she had worked four Saturdays in a row.
But Jake was right too.
He hadn’t had a free weekend since April.
Then I had an idea.
I asked Ben if he could work that Saturday, and he agreed.
In return, I gave him a Friday off.
Tina could go to the recital, and Jake could go to his concert.
The next morning, Tina brought donuts for everyone, and Jake made the coffee.
The store felt like a team again.
